title: Caveat Emptor – It’s Impossible To Judge Where You Are On Any Boom Path
author: Xebec
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

September’s WSTS Report saw July’s total semiconductor sales up 129.4 percent vs. July 2025, but down from last month’s record-breaking 144.2 percent growth.

The overall chip market continues to show treble-digit monthly annualised value growth rates, twice as large as the industry’s two previous record highs in June 2000 (59.3 percent) and January 2010 (66.6 percent). Prior to that, industry cyclical peaks maxed out in the 30-40 percent range.

The single biggest difference between this boom and all others is its razor-sharp focus on just a single, highly specialised AI infrastructure end market, with ASPs, not units, as its foundation for growth. All previous cycles were broadly-based and unit demand driven.

The single biggest common factor with all previous booms is the near zealous belief that this time was different and would not end in tears.

This denial is even more deep-rooted and passionate in the current boom, fueled by the transformational nature of AI and the productivity and application impact it will clearly have on society and the global economy.

Conventional AI wisdom emphasizes this transformational nature and, by association, its ability to sustain the current high chip-market growth rates, with ICs the main beneficiary, up 151.4 percent vs. July 2025

It conveniently ignores the unaffordable nature of AI-related chips in the broader semiconductor end market. The more mundane, non-AI chip market grew more sedately at around one tenth the headline level, with the Opto and Discrete sectors growing just 8.4 percent and 13.5 percent respectively.

Whilst we do not doubt AI’s longer-term transformational impact, and the end-market opportunities it will herald, we believe the current boom, emphasising infrastructure vs. end products, is not representative of the ultimate market demand.

We believe there will be a correction but acknowledge it is impossible to judge in advance precisely where we are on any boom path and, by implication, exactly when that correction will strike.

Only time will tell whether our cautionary view is warranted, and if we are wrong, you will read it here first. Meanwhile, enjoy the market growth numbers, but make plans … just in case.

Malcolm Penn
13 Sep 2026
